blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI applied to Health Insurance & Benefits. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Health payers sit between clinical reality and administrative machinery: prior authorization, coding integrity, quality programs and member experience all hinge on reading clinical evidence quickly and acting on it consistently — at HIPAA-grade privacy.

items: Coverage decisions cite policies inconsistently; member appeals overturn on documentation that was never surfaced.
Requests bounce for missing clinical evidence that exists in notes; turn-around times breach SLAs and clinicians revolt.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Generative AI Platform Engineering, Multimodal AI & Vision-Language Systems, Generative AI Platform Engineering from the Applied AI & Generative AI tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Prior authorization, Claims coding integrity, Quality/HEDIS reporting) on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — HIPAA among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Align AI to P&L lines and risk mandates — a sequenced portfolio, not a pile of pilots.
One governed platform, many GenAI products: retrieval, guardrails and cost control as shared services.
Own your models: tune, distill and operate LLMs with measurable quality, controlled cost and enforceable policy.
Coverage logic citing medical policy passages with provenance (appeals overturn rate down)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: policy, coverage and prior-claims context assembled per file with grounding (adjuster handling time down 30%). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
